In a 2.5D paper-based model, the nanofibers guide Neuro-2a cell organization and promote neurite-like extensions through topographical interactions. Building on these findings, a printable composite bioink comprising a gelatin/alginate liquid phase and gelatin microstrands is fabricated. The resulting inks exhibit shear-thinning behavior, rapid structural recovery, and sufficient mechanical stability for extrusion-based 3D bioprinting. Incorporation of SH-SY5Y cells generates viable and proliferative progenitor microtissues, with increasing gelatin microstrand content favoring neuronal-like morphologies. Integration of the gold nanofibers further enhances neuronal differentiation, as supported by cell morphology, immunostaining, and expression of neuronal markers, with differentiation occurring even in the absence of retinoic acid, a common chemical differentiation factor. Spatial separation of the gold nanofibers from the cells reduces this effect, highlighting the importance of direct cell-material interactions. Together, these results establish high-aspect-ratio gold nanofibers provide structural cues capable of promoting neuronal differentiation within 3D bioprinted tissues and provide a strategy for engineering neuron-like microtissues without relying exclusively on chemical differentiation agents.

item.title: Enhanced Spin-Forbidden Excitation of Ru(II) Polypyridyl Complexes for the Promotion of Red-Light Photocatalysis
item.description: Photoredox catalysis, mainly occurring under blue light, has emerged as an indispensable tool in modern organic synthesis. However, some limitations remain, mostly due to the high energy inherent to the irradiation wavelengths used. Red-light excitation of transition-metal photocatalysts is attractive for expanding the synthetic utility of visible-light photochemistry. Here, we report a strategy to enhance spin-forbidden red-light absorption in Ru(II) polypyridyl complexes through ligand tuning. [Ru(Br2-bpy)3](PF6)2 exhibits a substantially intensified spin-forbidden absorption band in the red region, with a molar extinction coefficient approximately 10-fold higher than that of [Ru(bpy)3]2+. The enhanced red-light absorption results in markedly improved photocatalytic activity under 660 nm irradiation in a range of electron- and energy-transfer transformations. Comparison with the parent complex demonstrates that modulation of the spin-forbidden absorption pathway can directly influence red-light photochemical reactivity. These findings support ligand modification as an effective approach for enhancing spin-forbidden excitation and provide a molecular design strategy for redlight-responsive Ru(II) photocatalysts, establishing Ru(II) polypyridyl complexes as an efficient family of photocatalysts activated via a spin-forbidden transition pathway.

item.title: Formamidine-Linked Covalent Organic Frameworks
item.description: Formamidine has been established as a versatile molecule in agriculture, organic solar cells, and as a ligand in organometallic catalysis. Despite, formamidine-based materials have remained largely unexplored due to challenges in achieving controlled polymerization. In this direction, we introduce a one-pot microwave-assisted diamine-orthoformate condensation strategy to synthesize formamidine-linked conjugated covalent organic frameworks (FOF-2 and FOF-3). Interestingly, the formamidine units of FOFs enable affinity towards urea, and that allowed us to use as metal-free electrocatalysts for the urea oxidation reaction (UOR) in alkaline media. FOF-2 demonstrates an onset potential value of 1.47 V (vs RHE) and a lower overpotential. The ordered microporous conjugated backbone facilitates charge and mass transport in FOFs. These findings demonstrate that metal-free FOFs can serve as a platform for UOR and open new directions toward organic framework-based electrocatalysts for sustainable energy conversion.

item.title: Defining Applicability Domains for Metal–Ligand Selectivity Prediction: Predictive Uncertainty vs. Molecular Similarity
item.description: Applicability domains are widely used to determine whether a machine-learning prediction can be trusted, yet they are commonly defined by similarity to the training data rather than by evidence that similarity predicts error. Here, we treat an applicability criterion as a testable claim and evaluate whether it identifies predictions with lower error than an equally sized random subset on a common held-out population. We test 23 criteria on a context-dependent metal–ligand selectivity problem, comparing molecular fingerprints, descriptor-space distances, learned embeddings, training support and predictive uncertainty. At 50% retention, predictive uncertainty reduces mean-of-pairs RMSE by 65%, compared with 32% for the best molecular distance and 18% for the best ligand-only distance. Fingerprint nearest-neighbour and learned-embedding distances provide no useful error ordering, whereas uncertainty remains informative after accounting for training support and predicted magnitude. In a prospective-style selection task, ranking ligands by their standardized predicted margin above a selectivity threshold increases single-ligand success from 0.639±0.035 under random selection to 0.831± 0.059. These results show that, at least for the context-dependent metal-ligand selectivity task studied here, structural similarity to the training data is not, by itself, evidence of predictive reliability in context-dependent molecular prediction. Applicability criteria can instead be treated as empirical hypotheses and tested directly against held-out error before being used to define reliable prediction regions or benchmark difficulty.

item.title: Application-Specific Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis of Source-Optimized Nanoparticle Textile Formulations: Trade-offs in Washing Durability, Antibacterial Performance, and Laboratory-Scale Raw-Material Cost
item.description: Nanoparticle-functionalized textiles offer antibacterial and self-cleaning functions, but their practical suitability is difficult to compare because laundering protocols, reported performance measures, and formulation costs vary across studies. This study develops an application-specific multi-criteria decision-analysis framework using harmonized secondary data from eight source-optimized TiO2-, ZnO-, Ag-, and hybrid-based textile formulations under a school sports-bib scenario. Washing durability and laboratory-scale raw-material cost were evaluated for all eight formulations, while antibacterial performance was included for the six formulations with sufficiently comparable data. Laundering results were converted to a common ten-reference-wash horizon, normalized criterion scores were evaluated across the full feasible weight space, and targeted sensitivity analyses examined uncertainty arising from washing normalization, incomplete Ag laundering conditions, sparse ZnO evidence, and possible cost underestimation. Under baseline conditions, Hybrid ZnO-TiO2 applied by padding-squeezing and Ag deposited through two-step grafting and reduction formed the Pareto frontier in both the two-and three-criterion models. The hybrid formulation was preferred under cost-oriented priorities, whereas the Ag formulation was favored when durability or antibacterial performance received greater weight. This principal decision structure remained stable across the tested uncertainty scenarios. In the Ag-excluded metal-oxide subset, Hybrid Padding-Squeezing remained the budget-sensitive option, while Hybrid In-Situ became more competitive when performance was prioritized. Substantial within-material variation indicated that formulation and deposition route were important sources of practical performance variation within the selected dataset. The framework provides a transparent method for translating heterogeneous published textile data into conditional, application-specific formulation decisions.

item.title: NEVPT2 Multiple Spawning Molecular Dynamics Simulations for Uracil
item.description: The quasidegenerate n-electron valence state second-order perturbation theory (QD-NEVPT2) for complete active space reference wavefunctions has been implemented in the OpenMolcas package. The implementation utilizes the efficient formulation of Kollmar et al. for the electronic energy, which is extended here to the calculation of analytic derivatives. To demonstrate its utility, the method is applied to classical and non-adiabatic molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of uracil. The non-adiabatic MD simulations describe the ultrafast deactivation of the initially excited bright ππ∗ state through the S2/S1 conical intersection, demonstrating the applicability of the method to photochemical processes. Furthermore, a machine learning-based analysis of the trajectory data extracts key geometrical parameters that are associated with the magnitude of the time-derivative coupling.

item.title: Tunable Aza-BODIPY Photocatalysts for Near-Infrared Metallaphotoredox Atom Transfer Radical Polymerization
item.description: The merger of photoredox and transition-metal catalysis has significantly advanced radical and redox transformations, yet its reliance on UV or visible light continues to limit applications in optically complex and spatially confined environments. Herein, we introduce a modular family of tetraaryl aza-boron-dipyrromethene (aza-BODIPY) organic photocatalysts (PCs) for near-infrared (NIR) metallaphotoredox atom transfer radical polymerization (ATRP). We systematically modulated peripheral electronics and core bromination, evaluating the dyes through quantum-chemical, electrochemical, and spectroscopic methods. This approach identified the key parameters governing catalytic performance: a delicate interplay between triplet-state accessibility, redox properties, and photostability. The optimized aza-BODIPY dye enables well-controlled ATRP of diverse acrylates and methacrylates at ultralow catalyst loadings, down to 5 ppm PC and 50 ppm copper complex. The system is further translated to open-air aqueous conditions, enabling rapid, high-throughput synthesis of water-soluble polymers in a 96-well plate format. Taking advantage of the enhanced penetration of NIR light, we demonstrate controlled polymerization through challenging physical barriers, including ex vivo tissue. Overall, this work defines design principles for far-red/NIR-absorbing aza-BODIPY PCs and expands the scope of NIR-mediated polymer synthesis to optically turbid, spatially restricted, and aqueous environments.

item.title: Beyond Materials Rankings: When Adsorption or Membranes Win for CO2/CH4 Separation
item.description: Choosing between adsorption and membranes for carbon dioxide removal from methane is often reduced to a contest between material metrics, even though an industrially meaningful answer emerges from the coupled material, flowsheet, pressure, composition, recovery, and economic context. Here we compare the technologies on a common process boundary, allowing each to select its process-optimal material, equipment size, and membrane architecture while meeting identical methane-product and recovery constraints. The resulting atlas spans 300 ARC–MOF adsorbents, 220 experimental polymers, and 864 matched biogas-and natural-gas-like scenarios. Among 676 mutually feasible cases, adsorption minimizes annualized cost in 73.4% and membranes in 26.6%; choosing the wrong technology incurs a median cost regret of 19.4%. Crucially, the boundary is not a single pressure threshold. Four pressurized-natural-gas slices exhibit clean adsorption–membrane–adsorption re-entry as the optimal material and membrane flowsheet switch with operating conditions. Material and architecture ablations isolate this mechanism. Cost-based choices disagree with energy, methane-loss, and footprint choices in 30.8–46.0% of paired comparisons, while cost and operational-climate choices disagree in 25.4%; joint uncertainty creates an explicit abstention region in 18.3% of boundary-focused cases. The framework converts high-throughput materials screening into conditional, auditable technology-selection rules and a compact agenda for cycle and mixed-gas validation under realistic process conditions and quantified uncertainty ranges.

item.title: PARAMAGNETIC SUPRAMOLECULAR POLYMERS OF METAL-METAL BONDED DIRUTHENIUM COMPLEXES
item.description: The self-assembly of paramagnetic molecular units into higher-order architectures remains a largely unexplored strategy for creating functional magnetic materials. Here we report the formation of supramolecular polymers from a metal-metal bonded diruthenium monomer. Variable-concentration NMR studies, including DOSY, demonstrate the chloride-driven self-assembly of monomeric species into linear aggregates in solution. Remarkably, magnetic measurements reveal that the paramagnetic character of the monomer is successfully transferred to the supramolecular polymer, giving rise to a magnetically active material. The comparison between monomeric and aggregated states shows that supramolecular organization modulates the magnetic properties through intermolecular interactions. This work establishes metal-metal-bonded diruthenium units as versatile building blocks for designing paramagnetic supramolecular material with emergent magnetic behavior

item.title: Next Generation NPK Slow Release Hydrogel Fertilizers: A Critical Review of Material Design, Performance, and Field Translation
item.description: Climate variability, water scarcity, declining soil quality, and inefficient fertilizer use are increasing the need for nutrient-delivery systems that support climate-resilient agriculture. Slow-release fertilizer hydrogels (SRFHs) are promising because they can retain water and control nutrient transport. This critical review examines SRFHs within conventional and enhanced-efficiency fertilizer strategies. It covers matrix, coated reservoir, and multilayer systems, along with their preparation methods and functional properties. The available evidence shows that polymer composition, crosslink density, pore structure, particle size, fertilizer loading, and environmental conditions affect swelling, mechanical behavior, and nutrient release. Important environmental factors include soil confinement, pH, ionic strength, and temperature. Kinetic models and response surface methodology can help explain release mechanisms and formulation trade-offs. Moisture-, pH-, and temperature-responsive systems may also support more adaptive nutrient delivery. However, high swelling or prolonged release in deionized water does not demonstrate improved nutrient uptake, crop yield, water-use efficiency, reduced nutrient loss, or environmental safety under field conditions. Translation is limited by inconsistent protocols, inadequate dose-matched controls, few multi-season trials, and limited evidence on degradation, residual materials, batch reproducibility, scale-up, and farm-level value. To address these gaps, this review proposes a target product profile that links crop, soil, and climate conditions with nutrient-specific release, mechanical service life, environmental fate, manufacturability, and economic performance. Model-guided responsive formulations could eventually be combined with sensor- and IoT-enabled monitoring for precision agriculture. However, this remains a prospective rather than field-validated approach. SRFHs should therefore be judged by reproducible and context-specific agronomic and environmental performance rather than maximum laboratory performance alone.

item.title: Direct-Write Printing of Freestanding Prussian Blue Analogue Fibers with Tunable Redox Potentials
item.description: Prussian blue (PB) and its analogues (PBAs) are attractive electrode materials for energy storage because of their chemical tunability, open-framework structures, fast ion transport, and rich redox chemistry. Yet, their practical implementation remains limited due to the challenging processability and the discrete set of redox potentials accessible through conventional compositions. Here, a 3D flow-focusing microfluidic strategy is used for directly synthesizing and printing freestanding PB and PBA composite fibers in a single step, coupling particle formation with their integration into an alginate/carbon-nanotube matrix. The method yields continuous, self-supporting fibers incorporating PB and multiple PBAs (Co, Ni, Cu, Zn), which can be directly written into functional electrode architectures and assembled into working energy storage cells. Beyond processability, the platform enables two complementary routes for voltage design: high-entropy PBAs, which access redox responses distinct from those of conventional single-metal PBAs, and spatially encoded fibers in which different PBAs are integrated within one fiber to generate intermediate and deliberately tuned electrochemical behavior. By exploiting the inherent spatial and temporal control afforded by microfluidic flow focusing, the approach establishes a versatile route toward printed, application-tailored PB and PBA electrodes with programmable operating voltages.

item.title: Case Studies of Homemorphic Isomerization: Interconversion of In/Out Isomers of Bicyclo[6.5.1]tetradecane and Related Bicyclic Hydrocarbons
item.description: Homeomorphic isomerization is equivalent to turning a molecule inside out in the same manner as a reversible article of clothing. Manifestations include the interconversion of (a) in,in and out,out isomers, or (b) in,out and out,in isomers of bicyclic molecules, but without inverting the configurations of the bridgehead atoms. In this preprint, this topological process is probed computationally for the title molecules. For the in,in/out,out manifold, the CH2 tether is able to transit through the CH(CH2)6CH tether with a barrier of ~26 kcal/mol, in good agreement with an experimental measurement. The geometries of the ground and transition states are analyzed in detail and the process of isomerization is visualized in animations.

item.title: Lipid-Phase Access Does Not Explain P-Glycoprotein Substrate Selection in Matched Pairs
item.description: The hydrophobic vacuum cleaner model holds that P-glycoprotein intercepts substrates within the lipid bilayer, which makes lipid-phase access to the transporter a candidate determinant of efflux, but the proposition has never been tested on compounds matched for the properties that otherwise dominate. We simulated nine matched molecular pairs—matched simultaneously on calculated lipophilicity, hydrogen-bond donors, polar surface area and molecular weight, and differing 5.9-to 30.1-fold in measured MDR1-MDCK efflux ratio—in a coarse-grained blood–brain barrier membrane containing human P-glycoprotein, and applied a pre-registered observable: enrichment E of substrate over non-substrate within 3.5 nm of the lateral portal axis. E bears no relation to efflux (ρ = −0.100, p = 0.80, n = 9), and the slope of unity predicted if access governed efflux lies outside the 95% interval [−0.51, +0.79], while five matched replicas put the measurement error at 3.65 times below the pair-to-pair spread, so the null is informative rather than underpowered. Selection is therefore decided after arrival at the transporter rather than during delivery to it.

item.title: Photochemical Aminomethylation of C(sp3)–H Bonds via Hydrogen Atom Transfer
item.description: Direct installation of an aminomethyl group onto aliphatic C–H bonds provides an attractive route to valuable amine-containing building blocks but remains challenging with conventional polar approaches. Here, we report a photochemical aminomethylation of C(sp3)–H bonds enabled by hydrogen atom transfer (HAT). Photoexcited benzophenone directly abstracts hydrogen from αamino, α-oxy, and α-thio C–H bonds, generating carbon-centered radicals that are intercepted by an in situ-formed N-protected formimine. This strategy provides direct access to protected vicinal diamines, amino alcohol derivatives, and related aminomethylated products without requiring prefunctionalization of the C–H donor. Notably, the C–H substrate can be employed as the limiting reagent, while selective radical generation suppresses overfunctionalization. Translation to continuous flow reduces reaction times from 20 h to 3 h, while improving yields for the investigated substrates, and enables scalable synthesis. Subsequent deprotection and functionalization further demonstrate the synthetic utility of the resulting aminomethylated products.

item.title: Catalytic C–O Bond Cleavage of Vinyl Ethers via Dehydrovinylation and Tandem Tishchenko Coupling
item.description: The cleavage of ether C–O bonds by transition-metal complexes has attracted considerable attention, but catalytic cleavage of vinyl ether C(sp²)–O bonds is largely unexplored. Herein we report the dehydrovinylation of alkyl vinyl ethers catalyzed by a pincer-ligated osmium complex. Primary alkyl vinyl ethers undergo C–O bond cleavage to afford ethylene and the corresponding aldehydes, which undergo tandem Tishchenko coupling to yield esters. Secondary alkyl vinyl ethers undergo dehydrovinylation to afford ethylene and ketones. Experimental observations and density functional theory calculations support a mechanism involving insertion of the vinyl ether C=C bond into an Os–H bond, followed by β-alkoxy elimination and β-hydride elimination to form the carbonyl product. These results establish a new mode of catalytic C(sp²)–O bond cleavage and demonstrate its application in a tandem dehydrovinylation–Tishchenko transformation.

item.title: Collective vibrational strong coupling triggers dissociation reaction by overcoming energy threshold
item.description: Ground-state reactions under vibrational strong coupling (VSC) have emerged as one of the central topics in polariton chemistry, yet how the energy redistribution under collective VSC translates into chemical reactivity remains an open question. Here we investigate vibrational predissociation in dilute ensembles of water trimers coupled to an optical cavity using full-dimensional cavity quasi-classical trajectory (cav-QCT) simulations with ab initio-quality potential-energy and dipole-moment surfaces. We demonstrate that collective VSC directly induces an otherwise energetically forbidden dissociation of the water trimer through cavity-mediated intermolecular VET. Remarkably, the enhancement of reactivity remains observable with increasing ensemble size despite reduced effective single-molecule light–matter coupling strength. Trajectory analyses identify collective energy transfer as the microscopic mechanism and reveal largely consistent quantum-state distributions of the reaction products. These findings establish a microscopic link between collective polaritonic energy transport and chemical reactivity, and suggest collective VSC as a route toward simultaneously manipulating reactivity and preserving product-state selectivity.

item.title: A Scalable One-Pot Strategy for Porphyrin Metal–Organic Frameworks via In situ Linker Synthesis
item.description: Porphyrin metal–organic frameworks (pMOFs) are highly versatile materials for catalysis, energy, and environmental applications, yet their widespread use is limited by the cost and multistep synthesis of porphyrin linkers. Here, we report a one-pot synthetic strategy that integrates porphyrin formation and MOF crystallization, enabling the direct assembly of zirconium-based pMOFs from simple molecular precursors. This approach eliminates the need for linker isolation and purification, significantly reducing synthetic complexity and resource consumption. The method is demonstrated for the benchmark framework PCN-224 and its zinc metalloporphyrin analogue, yielding crystalline, porous materials at multigram scale. Notably, the resulting materials exhibit enhanced mesoporosity, which improves mass transport and enables superior adsorption of large organic dyes, despite lower BET surface areas compared to conventionally synthesized analogues. Importantly, we further demonstrate the generality of this approach by synthesizing USTC-9(Fe), a framework with distinct metal nodes and porphyrin linker geometry. This work establishes a versatile platform for coupling complex linker synthesis with framework assembly, offering a sustainable and scalable route to functional pMOFs and broadening the scope of in situ linker formation in reticular chemistry.

item.title: Atomic-Scale Insights into the Surface Chemistry, Surface Stability, and Floatability of Spodumene and Montebrasite with Fatty Acid Collectors
item.description: Spodumene and montebrasite are minerals that contain significant quantities of lithium and are often found together in phosphate-rich lithium pegmatites. Separating these two minerals by flotation is key to efficient downstream lithium extraction from each. Understanding the crystal and surface properties of both minerals is an important step towards their separation by flotation. We present a systematic study of the surface properties of spodumene and montebrasite, and their interactions with fatty acid collectors, using density functional theory calculations. Our results showed that, for montebrasite, the most dominant surfaces were (110) ≈ (012̅) > (102̅) > (12̅0) > (212̅), with (110) ≈ (012̅) being the most represented (56 %). The Al-terminated (110) surface was the dominant surface on spodumene, accounting for 70 % of the crystal surface area, followed by (111̅) > (111) > (101̅) > (001), consistent with available experimental data. The Wulff equilibrium morphology showed that both minerals are elongated/prismatic, consistent with their naturally occurring crystals, but spodumene is less reactive to flotation reagents than montebrasite. Surface electronic density of states showed that Li and Al states dominate the bottom of the conduction band of spodumene (110) and montebrasite (110) and are available to hybridize with oxygen states of the COO- functional group of fatty acid collectors. Energetics calculations show that both minerals interact with fatty acid collectors via surface Al and Li, but more strongly for montebrasite than spodumene (–18.6 kcal/mol vs +11.05 kcal/mol). Therefore, montebrasite is more floatable with fatty acid collectors than spodumene, making it convenient to separate these two minerals by first recovering montebrasite to the flotation concentrate, resulting in a spodumene-enriched tailings product. Less favorable adsorption energies explain the need to activate/pretreat spodumene before flotation to overcome the energy barrier for fatty-acid adsorption, with spodumene activation by high-density conditioning performed only after montebrasite flotation. This study further demonstrates that the interaction energy of fatty acids with mineral surfaces does not depend on chain length, regardless of mineral type. Our findings open a new direction for efficient lithium production from phosphate-rich lithium pegmatites by generating a montebrasite concentrate while simultaneously upgrading the feed to the spodumene flotation circuit.

item.title: Surface hydroxyls act as key intermediates in the selective oxidative dehydrogenation of 2-propanol on Co3O4
item.description: Transition-metal oxides typically catalyze aerobic oxidation reactions with high activity even at low temperatures, but rarely with high selectivity. Owing to the complexity of competing surface processes on such catalysts, the rational design of selective low-temperature catalysts still requires a deeper mechanistic understanding of the active surface and reaction intermediates. In this work, we combine operando modulation-excitation infrared spectroscopy with density functional theory and molecular dynamics to mechanistically investigate 2-propanol oxidation over Co3O4 with a focus on surface hydroxyls, acting as hydrogen acceptors during alcohol adsorption. We identify two chemically distinct hydroxyl populations: linear hydroxyls, which actively participate in acetone formation and can be considered part of the active surface ensemble, and bridged hydroxyls, which behave largely as spectators. Together, these results provide a molecular-level mechanistic picture of alcohol oxidation on Co3O4 and establish the dynamic role of surface hydroxyl species as active players in heterogeneous oxidation catalysis.

item.title: Rational construction of semi-clathrate-like water networks on engineered ferritin cages
item.description: Understanding and controlling the organization of water at molecular interfaces is a longstanding goal in both biological and materials sciences, as it controls the biophysical properties of the surfaces. For example, semi-clathrate waters containing polygonal hydrogen-bonded water clusters found in some antifreeze proteins (AFPs), are thought to play key roles in interacting with ice. Despite this significance, the lack of well-defined design principles makes it difficult to rationally construct such ordered hydration architectures. Here, we report the rational construction of a semiclathrate-like water network in an engineered ferritin cage. We designed a series of alanine (Ala) mutants on the internal surface of the ferritin cage and analyzed the formation of semi-clathratelike water networks using X-ray crystal structure analysis. Our results indicate that the continuous hydrophobic surface formed by the Ala mutation organizes water molecules on its surface, forming semi-clathrate-like water networks. Specific hydrogen-bonding networks involving the main-chain carbonyl group were found to play a key role in initiating the formation of semi-clathrate-like water networks. These findings are significant for organizing water molecules on the protein surface to control biophysical properties.

item.title: CAN it work? Using hydroxyethyl acrylate or methacrylate to turn epoxy-amine thermosets into covalent adaptable network materials.
item.description: Epoxy-amine thermosets can be converted into covalent adaptable networks (CANs) by adding β-aminoester-based curing agents to the formulation. This is achieved by utilizing commercially available di- or trifunctional acrylate monomers, which react with the amine component via an aza-Michael addition. Consequently, this approach is inherently scalable and holds high industrial relevance. In this study, the fundamental applicability of two commodity chemicals—namely 2-hydroxyethyl acrylate (HEA) and 2-hydroxyethyl methacrylate (HEMA)—for this purpose is investigated, aiming to provide an additional handle to mitigate the rapid viscosity increase of the formulations. Using a model epoxy resin consisting of bisphenol A diglycidyl ether (DGEBA) and 1,3-bis(aminomethyl)cyclohexane (BAC), it was demonstrated that a Lewis-base catalyst (1-methylimidazole) is necessary to incorporate the hydroxy groups of HEA and HEMA into the network. Contrary to expectations, this incorporation proceeds predominantly through a condensation reaction that liberates ethylene glycol. Finally, a formulation consisting of 1 equiv. DGEBA, 0.5 equiv. BAC, 1 equiv. HEA, and 0.025 equiv. 1-methylimidazole was found to offer a good compromise, providing both satisfactory reprocessability and a sufficiently high glass transition temperature (74 °C). Compared to a reference formulation made with a trifunctional acrylate monomer, the CAN made with HEA is characterized by a lower glass transition temperature, a similar flow activation energy, a lower storage modulus, and distinctly longer relaxation times. Both acrylate-based CAN materials aged under thermal stress, which resulted in higher storage moduli and glass transition temperatures upon reprocessing. A protocol for characterizing such modulus changes under thermal stress is suggested, consisting of performing repeated frequency sweeps for at least 1 h at temperatures slightly exceeding the maximum temperature of the stress relaxation measurements.

item.title: Lithium Plating-Induced Fracture of Individual Graphite Platelets Revealed by Operando
item.description: Lithium plating is a key barrier to achieving faster charging of lithium-ion batteries; however, fundamental and nanoscale understanding of plating is still being developed, largely due to the dynamic nature of the process. Here, we perform operando electrochemical atomic force microscopy on individual graphite platelets to observe the morphology evolution of plated lithium and graphite electrodes simultaneously. We observe plating-induced fracture of the graphite platelets even in the absence of a porous electrode structure. Unexpectedly, fracture occurs through preferential lithium deposition beneath the particle surface despite lithium-ion transport limitations, pointing to lithium in graphite as the lithium source. Our findings deepen the understanding of the lithium plating process and offer pathways to improvement for fast-charged negative electrodes.

item.title: Zwitterionic Acyl Anion Equivalents from Carboxylic Acids via Acylsulfonylhydrazides: A Practical Organocatalytic Umpolung
item.description: The development of mild and practical acyl anion equivalents remains a cornerstone challenge in modern organic synthesis, as traditional umpolung strategies often rely on moisture-sensitive reagents, strong bases, or specialized N-heterocyclic carbene catalysts. Here we report that readily available N,N-acylsulfonylhydrazides serve as efficient acyl anion surrogates under operationally simple organocatalytic conditions. Using DMAP as a nucleophilic catalyst, these stable hydrazide precursors readily provide acylation products of a wide range of carbon electrophiles, including aromatic and aliphatic aldehydes, activated ketones, olefins, and imines. Mechanistic investigations, supported by DFT calculations and HRMS analysis, reveal an unconventional pathway wherein DMAP adds to the acyldiazene intermediate, triggering nitrogen extrusion and generating a zwitterionic nucleophile. This dual role of DMAP in enhancing both the stability and nucleophilicity of the reactive species circumvents the hydroxycarbene rearrangement pathway, offering a practical and scalable alternative to existing acyl anion methodologies.

item.title: Data-driven discovery of pH-dependent surfactant behavior in a peptide amphiphile library
item.description: Developing bio-based formulations is essential for reducing the environmental impact of modern surfactants. Peptide amphiphile (PA) surfactants offer a modular platform for developing materials with tailored structures and functions, making them highly attractive to replace existing petrochemical surfactants. However, rationally designing peptide sequences with predictable and tunable surface activity remains challenging. Existing sequence-based models primarily target aggregation and antimicrobial activity and cannot predict surface activity or account for environmental conditions such as pH and temperature. To address this shortcoming, we combine experimental and computational approaches to investigate sequence–property relationships of PAs. We employ automated experimental workflows to generate a consistent dataset of PA surface tension across a range of pHs. Our analyses reveal that the presence of proline most strongly induces surface activity at all pHs. Positively charged residues such as lysine and arginine more strongly introduce surface activity than negatively charged residues. Experimental validation of a machine learning classifier trained on the data collected for our library showed that the machine learning model correctly predicts surface activity in 97% of the sampled predicted surface active sequences. Thereby, we show that machine learning models trained on our dataset generalize across the sequence space, and enable targeted design of surface active PAs in diverse environments.

item.title: A dimension staircase for orientational heat capacity: nature skips the 3/2 rung
item.description: The low-temperature orientational heat capacity of an interacting multipole pair is conventionally taken to be two-valued: 3/2 kB for axially symmetric moments and 2 kB otherwise. Here I evaluate it for all 101,666,280 molecular geometries of the OMol25 dataset and show that this is the bottom rung of a staircase: the exponent is a count, not a case split, γ = Cv / kB = Σi 1/pi, which for two rigid nonlinear molecules is exactly γ= D / 2 and leaves only the rungs 3/2, 2 and 5/2. Of 11,325,000 pairs drawn uniformly from the whole dataset none occupies the 3/2 rung (P < 3.26 x 10-7; structural bound 4.187 x 10-7), and the rest split 12.05% and 87.95% between γ= 2 and 5/2, so nearly the whole molecular world shares one coefficient: 5/2 kB = 20.79 J mol-1 K-1 per mole of pairs. The 3/2 rung is deleted rather than thermally suppressed (a 0.129 Å C-H bending amplitude exceeds the 0.1 Å scale at which a C3v rotor saturates its axiality defect), so no temperature recovers it.

item.title: Advancing Targeted Nanoparticle mRNA Delivery Using Machine Learning
Resolving Month-Long Nanostructural Evolution in Degrading Anion Exchange Membranes
item.description: Chemical degradation reshapes the hydrated ion-transport channels of anion exchange membranes (AEMs), but conventional aging measurements do not reveal how their nanostructure evolves toward functional failure. Here we resolve this structural evolution using high-resolution kinetic Monte Carlo (kMC) simulations. The simulations are calibrated to reproduce the experimental ion exchange capacity (IEC) and water uptake (WU) over a month degradation of a PPO-TEA membrane. The ionomer-peak position remains essentially unchanged even after 70% cation loss, while the water channels narrow from approximately 0.8 to 0.6 nm and progressively fragment. The hydrated network loses percolation at a critical hydrophilic volume fraction 𝜙!≈ 0.26, close to the threshold (𝜙!≈ 0.25) inferred from experimental conductivity using a percolation power law. Two complementary descriptions, a percolation law and a connected-carrier model, reproduce the normalized conductivity decay without using conductivity to calibrate the degradation kinetics. These results link conductivity failure to the loss of connected transport pathways within a membrane that retains its characteristic phase-separation length scale. The structural predictions are similar for two kinetic models with different dependencies on local hydration. Thus, a persistent ionomer-peak position can conceal substantial deterioration of the ion-transport network. Resolving channel connectivity along the aging trajectory provides a structural measure of membrane durability that complements conventional characterization of phase separation.

item.title: The Dopant Cage Sets the Phonon Count of Lanthanide Emitters
item.description: Multiphonon relaxation decides whether a lanthanide ion emits light or heats its host. Since 1968 it has been predicted from the host’s maximum phonon energy, although the excitation resides on a single ion. First-principles force constants and five decades of relaxation measurements show that the accepting vibration is the stretch of the dopant’s coordination cage, a site property set by local chemistry. Aliovalent substitution stiffens the cage by up to 27%, and across seven halide hosts the cage frequency departs from the host frequency by −21% to +19%. It predicts measured effective phonon frequencies three times more accurately than the host frequency, and in its quanta the seven energy-gap laws share one room-temperature slope. The site-resolved laws map the lattice limits of optical refrigeration from 2 to 6 µm. The phonon count of a lanthanide emitter becomes a site property that chemistry can tune and theory can compute before synthesis.

item.title: Diverse Remote Difunctionalization of Enyne-type Propargylic Carbonates: Regio-, Chemo-, and Stereoselective Access to Highly Functionalized Multisubstituted 1,3-Dienes
item.description: Herein, we report the first catalytic heterodifunctionalization and homodifunctionalization of readily available 1-substituted enyne-type propargylic derivatives, proceeding via a multicomponent remote C2,C5-addition/substitution pathway. This palladium-catalyzed protocol enables the modular and straightforward assembly of tri-, tetra-, and penta-substituted 1,3-dienes with diverse functional groups from two heteroatom nucleophiles or one heteroatom nucleophile and one carbon nucleophile. The reaction exhibits high chemo-, regio-, and stereoselectivity, accommodates a broad spectrum of O-, N-, S-, and C-nucleophiles, and delivers highly substituted (Z, E)-1,3-dienes with precise stereocontrol. Notably, switching from O- to S-nucleophiles triggers a nucleophile-directed stereodivergence. The synthetic utility is further demonstrated through diverse downstream transformations, efficient synthesis of bioactive molecules, and late-stage functionalization of natural products. Mechanistic studies reveal the involvement of heteroatom-containing pentacoordinate π-allyl palladium and π-alkynyl palladium intermediates in this heterodifunctionalization process.

item.title: Treatise on Present Practice and Perspectives of MDGC
item.description: The state of affairs of multidimensional gas chromatography (MDGC) at present is no more than an implementation of a two-dimensional form (2D-GC) reducing its scope to the setup known as GCxGC. Introduced in 1991 with great expectation, however, GCxGC still happen to fall short of realizing the anticipated capabilities despite continuous efforts made over the elapsed 35 years. This got quantitative formulation in regard of separation performance as early as 2008, proving that it failed to be competitive with a well-governed 1D-GC. The present paper highlights further limitations of GCxGC: inadequate operation burdened with shortcomings are presented via examples taken from GCxGC literature; crowning the list with the inability to meet fundamental requirement that if a compound can be analyzed by 1D-GC it must remain analyzable by MDGC. The repertoire of the intertwining issues, each of which unavoidably rigs or even hamstrings the others, highlights that GCxGC has a built-in self-limiting feature. Attempts to overcome confinements via loosening the binding conditions turned GCxGC back to the form it emerged from decades ago, yet without getting rid of the hampering curbs. The unfavorable overall picture forces to consider viabilities of other concepts, with focus on avoiding errors and pitfalls of GCxGC while fulfilling basic requirements of MDGC. In our view, there are two alternatives. One is ZGC, principle of which was introduced in 1989, requirements and potential of which are presented here in more detail; the other is a concept called Quantum-GC, which is presented as an introductory approach.

item.title: An alternative equation for effective nuclear charge that is applicable to all atoms
item.description: Although the advent of ionization energies predated Slater’s rule, there was unawareness of the utilitarian value of the former for the computation of effective nuclear charge (ENC for short) until recently and in this research. The study aimed to derive another equation in which the average ionization energies of hydrogen and any other multielectron atom are independent variables. The objective was to answer the question in the literature that states, "Are Slater’s Rules the Best Approach for Calculating Effective Nuclear Charge for Undergraduates?" (Moore & Birnbaum, 2014) and compare the graphical portrayal of chemical periodicity between outcomes using data generated using Slater's rules for some elements and data generated in this research. By exploring theoretical and computational methods and the data in the literature, the study showed that ENC (1.34458-3.32446) for the first 30 elements computed using the 2021 CODATA fine structure constant (FSC, for short) was higher than those (1.34402-3.32309) without it; however, the equation containing the computed FSC using e^2/20hc and other equations gave the same value of ENC. The use of Slater’s result (atomic radii) for the computation of ENC (1.29859-5.06996) and average ionization energy, IE (553.21-2108.13 kJ), gave higher values than other methods. All plots using Slater’s values of ENC and IE versus atomic number (Z) did not show chemical periodicity (greater linearity), unlike the use of other values (less linearity or lower R^2). The use of Slater’s result (atomic radii) for the computation of ENC (1.29859-5.06996) and average ionization energy, IE (553.21-2108.13 kJ), gave higher values than other methods. All plots using Slater’s values of ENC and IE versus Z did not show chemical periodicity (greater linearity), unlike the use of other values (less linearity or lower R^2). The new equation was derived, and with earlier equations, ENC can be accurately computed; they should therefore be part of the school curriculum at all levels without ceasing to teach Slater’s rule, which is not the best approach. A future study should include 30 other elements of the periodic table.

item.title: Data-Driven Approach to Predicting Durability and Property Retention in Polymer Matrix Composites
item.description: Predicting the long-term performance of reinforced polymer composites from short-duration accelerated aging data remains a central challenge in composite durability engineering. This work presents a data-driven kinetic and mechanical-performance characterization of a glass-flake reinforced unsaturated polyester composite exposed to deionized water at 20, 40, 60 and 80 °C for up to 14.5 months, integrating long-term gravimetric sorption, flexural testing, and dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA), including substantial portions of the dataset that have not previously been analyzed or reported. The initial moisture sorption rate constant obeys an Arrhenius relationship across all four temperatures (activation energy Ea = 45.1 kJ/mol, R2 = 0.97), providing a kinetic basis for estimating uptake behavior within the tested temperature range. Extended gravimetric monitoring reveals a two stage hygrothermal response: an initial Fickian-like uptake stage reaching an apparent plateau (4.4-7.5 wt% depending on temperature and replicate), followed by a degradation-associated mass-loss stage, with weight gain at 60 °C falling from a 4.5% plateau to 1.8% after 14.5 months, and markedly greater coupon-to-coupon variability at 80 °C. Flexural modulus and strength retention under wet conditions (22-50% and 28-60% of dry values, respectively) is reported across all four temperatures at 2 and 6 months, alongside DMA glass transition temperature data showing an initial rise with exposure temperature followed by a decrease at 80 °C. No meaningful relationship between initial moisture sorption kinetics and 2-month mechanical retention could be established from the present four temperature-matched averages (Pearson r = 0.43, n = 4; retention is non-monotonic in ln(k)); the 6-month data instead indicate that degradation kinetics and exposure duration, rather than the initial sorption rate, are what track mechanical performance loss. The study does not establish a validated model for predicting mechanical-property retention; rather, it provides a quantitative experimental basis and structured dataset for future data-driven and machine-learning-based durability models of this and structurally similar glass-flake-reinforced polyester and related polymer matrix composite systems.

item.title: Enabling Optoelectronics in Cu2S/Co9S8 Heteroassembly
item.description: Semiconductor heteroassembly can integrate complementary properties through nanoscale interfaces, but structural integration alone does not necessarily yield optoelectronic functionality. Here, we demonstrate an optoelectronically active Cu2S/Co9S8 heteroassembly for photodetection, obtained through higher-temperature nucleation and growth conditions that may promote enhanced crystallization and structural ordering of Co9S8. Structural characterization reveals crystalline Cu2S nanostructures decorated with dense 3–5 nm Co9S8 nanocrystallites, providing extensive interfacial contact. HRTEM, electron diffraction, XRD, and elemental mapping confirm the coexistence and spatial integration of the two phases. Controlled antisolvent processing reduces residual organic content and enables formation of uniform films. A vertical Cu2S/Co9S8/n-Si device exhibits broadband photoresponse with rise and fall times of 2.7 and 2.3 s, respectively. At 2 V bias, the device achieves a responsivity of 1.93 mA W-1 and a shot-noise-limited detectivity of 6.3 × 107 Jones. The bias-dependent response is attributed to field-assisted photocarrier separation and extraction, with the Cu2S/n-Si junction and Cu2S/Co9S8 interfaces influencing carrier transport. These results highlight the combined importance of structural ordering and interfacial architecture in converting nanoscale heteroassembly into functional optoelectronic devices.

item.title: Transformation product bottleneck: Photo-recalcitrance of rotenolone limits the aquatic degradation of rotenone in a temperature-dependent manner
item.description: The environmental fate and toxicity of transformation products (TPs) are frequently overlooked. However, in many cases, TPs are functional analogs that exhibit similar, and often greater, toxicity as the parent compound. In cases where the TP is persistent in the environment, the rate of TP degradation can influence the overall environmental fate. Rotenolone (12𝛼-hydroxy-rotenone, ROH) is the primary TP of rotenone (ROT), a pesticide utilized ubiquitously and highly popular in cold regions. Both ROT and ROH are mitochondrial NADH inhibitors, however ROH is more persistent than ROT and remains unregulated. 2 This work investigated the aquatic photochemical pathways and transformation products of ROH, including simulated Subarctic (low-temperature) conditions. Given that ROT degradation is driven by photolysis, we hypothesized that inhibited photochemical activity of ROH accounts for its persistence. Our results suggest ROH persistence is largely attributed to significantly reduced triplet state lifetimes, absorbance, and apparent quantum yields. Temperature was identified as a significant driver of ROH photolysis, accelerating the direct photochemical transformation rate, with half-lives ranging from approximately 115 h (6 °C) to 66 h (19 °C). This suggests that the cool temperatures of Subarctic surface waters further contribute to ROH persistence. Degradation was accelerated in the presence of chromophoric dissolved organic matter (CDOM); Fenton experiments confirmed ROH reacts with hydroxyl radical at near diffusion-limited rates (2.9×1010 ± 1.1×109 M-1 s-1 at 20 °C). Nontarget analysis of ROH photoproducts revealed novel transformation intermediates not previously identified. These were observed to further transform to smaller products, suggesting that ROH photochemical transformation represents the final step in detoxification. Thus, the photochemical recalcitrance of ROH is involved in limiting the detoxification of ROT following aquatic pesticidal use. These results strongly suggest including ROH monitoring during ROT pesticide applications.

item.title: Molecular Symmetry Decomposition by Graph Automorphism: Fast, Symmetry-Aware RMSD, Structure Alignment, and Canonical Atom Ranks
item.description: The root-mean-square deviation (RMSD) is among the most widely used metrics in computational chemistry. However, computing a chemically meaningful RMSD requires solving a combinatorial “atom mapping” problem: finding the RMSD-minimizing and chemically acceptable correspondence between atoms in two structures. Existing methods force a trade-off. Graph-isomorphism enumeration is exact but can be computationally prohibitive. The faster (cubic scaling with molecular size) Hungarian assignment algorithm disregards the bonding topology and can return chemically invalid mappings and spuriously low RMSD values. We eliminate this trade-off by recasting the assignment problem in the language of graph automorphism, where the bond-preserving permutations form a group whose internal structure (orbits, stabilizers, and product decompositions) mirrors molecular topology. This yields a complete classification of molecular graph symmetry into coupled core and independent peripheral symmetry (falling into exactly two graph-theoretic classes), reducing the search from a product of local symmetries to a sum. The resulting algorithm, snapRMSD, produces assignments that are bond-preserving by construction and recovers the global RMSD minimum under mild conditions satisfied by most molecular structures. We demonstrate that snapRMSD is significantly faster than existing methods, often by orders of magnitude. As a byproduct, the same machinery yields exact canonical atom ranks, a rigorous alternative to the refinement heuristics used since the 1960s.

item.title: Direct Mechanochemical Aryl Amination of Polystyrene for Creep Resistant Imine Elastomers
item.description: Imine-based covalent adaptable networks (CANs) hold promise for the development of recyclable thermoset materials, but due to low barriers for dynamic exchange, such networks typically suffer from significant material creep. Incorporating linear polymers into imine CANs can improve creep resistance by introducing physical crosslinks, while reactive variants further mitigate through chemical crosslinks. Herein, we directly aminate polystyrene (up to 1.1 mol%) using ball mill grinding mechanochemistry with liquid-assisted grinding for inclusion into dynamic materials. This post-polymerization modification technique allows us to avoid excess solvent while preserving high molar mass. Incorporating aminated PS (aPS) in representative polyimine elastomers enhances creep resistance relative to unmodified PS, while generally maintaining comparable mechanical properties. These findings establish waste PS grafted with low densities of reactive primary amines as an effective additive for improving deformation resistance in polyimines, thus offering a route to give post-consumer plastic waste renewed value.

item.title: Beyond Bulk Grade: Mineral–Flow Accessibility Controls Pore-Scale Copper Recovery
item.description: Mineral dissolution in porous media is driven by fluid flow, solute transport, and geochemical reactions, yet reactive transport models commonly use bulk mineral abundance and specific surface area as proxies for mineral reactivity. This neglects a key constraint: dissolution occurs only where reactants can access minerals through connected fluid-flow pathways. Here, we use pore-scale PFLOTRAN simulations of acid-driven chrysocolla dissolution to isolate the effect of mineral accessibility at fixed initial mineral volume fraction. Across pore-network ensembles and flow–reaction conditions, copper recovery varied substantially (9–21%) despite identical bulk copper content. Recovery depended on the fraction of mineral accessible to connected flow and on mineral proximity to inlet-connected pores, even when cumulative pore volumes flushed during the 48 h acid pulse were nearly identical. In contrast, Péclet and Damköhler numbers characterized transport–reaction regimes but did not uniquely predict copper recovery because they do not encode pore-scale accessibility. An accessibility-weighted pore-volume metric combined with intrinsic dissolution kinetics explained recovery with R2 ≈ 0.95. Thus, our results show that mineral–flow accessibility and reaction kinetics jointly control pore-scale copper recovery and provide a physically interpretable basis for accessibility-aware reactive transport upscaling.

item.title: 3D DLP Printing of Multi-Responsive Cellulose Derivatives with Tunable Structural Color
item.description: Polymer systems exhibiting structural color represent a promising class of materials for 3D printing due to their capability to adapt their properties in response to external stimuli. Hydroxypropyl cellulose (HPC) stands out for its ability to form cholesteric liquid crystalline phases that exhibit vivid structural colors. In this work, we introduce a digital light processing strategy to fabricate complex 3D structures with tunable, stimuli-responsive structural color using methacrylated HPC (HPC-MA). By formulating an aqueous ink system containing 58 to 70 wt% HPC-MA and establishing a pre-print equilibration protocol, cholesteric order is developed and covalently locked into the printed architecture via photopolymerization. The resulting 3D printed structures display bright, iridescent structural colors, tunable within the entire visible spectrum. The thermoresponsive properties of the printed structures are investigated both in a dried and a water-swollen state. Notably, the thermochromic behavior exhibits opposing trends in both environments with increasing temperature inducing a redshift in the dry state but a blueshift in the aqueous state. Finally, we demonstrate the practical utility of this approach in zero-power visual humidity sensing and biomimetic adaptive camouflage. The integration of structural color, stimuli-responsiveness, and 3D geometric freedom opens avenues towards next-generation 4D printing, adaptive materials, and autonomous sensing.

item.title: Synthesis of Large-area Two-Dimension Metal-Organic Framework Films via Chemical Vapour Deposition
item.description: Synthesizing uniform and large-are two-dimensional (2D) metal-organic framework (MOF) films directly on substrates is highly desirable and important for MOF-based electronics, but it still remains great challenge. Here, a simple chemical vapour deposition (CVD) growth strategy with controllable-thickness and large-area capabilities has been developed to directly prepare them on substrates, in which 2,3,6,7,10,11-hexahydroxytriphenylene (HHTP) ligand films pre-deposited on substrates react with copper (II) acetylacetonate (Cu(acac)2) vapor, resulting the structure transformation from small molecule thin film to Cu3(HHTP)2 MOF films. The MOF films have high crystalline quality with uniform surface, large area (4 inches wafer) and controllable thickness (15 nm to 100 nm). And Replacing Cu(acac)2 with nickel (II) acetylacetonate (Ni(acac)2) and platinum (II) acetylacetonate (Pt(acac)2) as metal ion source, the method can also be used to synthesize uniform Ni3(HHTP)2 and Pt3(HHTP)2 MOF films, suggesting the generic applicability of this method. When employed the Cu3(HHTP)2 MOF films as an active material for optoelectronic devices, it simulates light-stimulated and synaptic memory properties, making it exhibit promising application in artificial biological synapse.

item.title: Spirocyclic Azetidines as Lactam Bioisosteres in Isoindolinones Through Facile C1 Stitching Enabled by Dual Energy- and Electron-Transfer Photocatalysis
item.description: Bioisosteric replacement of nitrogen-containing cyclic structures with smaller, more conformationally rigid ring systems such as azetidines and spirocyclic azetidines has emerged as an effective strategy to improve the physicochemical and pharmacokinetic profiles of nitrogen-bearing drug candidates. Despite extensive studies, the use of spirocyclic azetidines as bioisosteres has been limited to simple ring systems and has not been extended to medicinally relevant complex pharmacophores. Herein, we introduce benzo-fused spirocyclic azetidines as three-dimensional bioisosteres of lactam moieties in isoindolinones, significant structural motifs present in >40,000 bioactive compounds. Our synthetic strategy is to “stitch” in one step a broad range of oxadiazoline carbene precursors and substituted 1-azabicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (ABBs), thus accessing structurally diverse spirocyclic azetidines. This reaction is mechanistically novel, merging strain-release activation of ABB with a dual energy-transfer/single-electron-transfer photocatalytic cascade, enabling formal C1-insertion under mild conditions. The physicochemical and metabolic profiling suggests that these spirocyclic azetidine bioisosteres retain key physicochemical properties while improving metabolic stability. Moreover, docking studies indicate conserved recognition with the potential for interaction rewiring at selected targets. Given the ubiquitous presence of lactam and amide-containing motifs in bioactive molecules and drug candidates, this work opens new avenues for drug discovery and clinical development.

item.title: Following Nature’s Lead – Pillar[n]arene Phosphates as Versatile Molecular Hosts
item.description: Phosphates are ubiquitous natural recognition motifs. Their charge, hydrogen bonding, variable substitution, and reversible enzymatic installation uniquely enable complex tasks in Biology. However, they are not used extensively in supramolecular systems. Herein, we combine Nature’s modulator with supramolecular rational design, creating rim-functionalised pillar[n]arene phosphates, which act as highaffinity molecular hosts. Using robust phosphoramidite chemistry, we prepared P5Max and P6Max, based on pillar[5]arene and pillar[6]arene cores in four high yielding steps. We developed a high-throughput fluorescence displacement assay enabling us to explore a biologically focused screening panel and so rapidly investigate the recognition properties of our new hosts. P5Max and P6Max bind a series of structurally diverse chemotherapies, neuromuscular blockade agents, anaesthetics and antibiotics, with P6Max proving the more general host. We used functional assays to explore P6Max’s ability to control the biological effect of different drug classes, including highly toxic chemotherapy drugs and antibiotics. The use of high-throughput assays in host-guest systems provides a simple, rapid, and scalable route to translating supramolecular interactions to functional effect.

item.title: FMS2Lib: A Machine Learning-Ready Tandem Mass Spectral Library for Nontargeted Analysis of Non-conventional PFAS
item.description: Nontargeted identification of non-conventional per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), including fluorinated pharmaceuticals and pesticides, remains challenging. Existing machine learning models for nontargeted analysis, primarily trained on tandem mass spectra of nonfluorinated compounds, may not generalize well to non-conventional PFAS because of their distinct mass spectrometric chemistry. Here, we established FMS2Lib, an experimental tandem mass spectral library containing 34,686 fluorinated drug-like compounds (F1-4), to support machine learning-based nontargeted PFAS analysis. We demonstrated that training with FMS2Lib substantially improved the performance of existing models for both molecular formula prediction and structure annotation. We further applied these models to identify PFAS in passive samplers from wastewater effluents and surface waters and in high-throughput laboratory biotransformation experiments, revealing dozens of non-conventional PFAS and their biotransformation products. Collectively, FMS2Lib addresses a major data bottleneck in machine learning-based nontargeted analysis of non-conventional PFAS.

item.title: Mechanistic basis of μ-opioid receptor allosteric modulation from molecular simulations
item.description: The μ-opioid receptor (μOR) is a central mediator of analgesia and opioid-induced adverse effects, yet the molecular basis by which allosteric modulators reshape receptor signaling remains poorly understood. Here, we integrate all-atom molecular dynamics with unbinding kinetics simulations to resolve the mechanistic basis of positive and negative allosteric modulation of μOR. We show that the positive allosteric modulator BMS-986122 enhances signaling not through uniform stabilization of canonical active microswitches, but by selectively remodeling the sodium pocket and, critically, stabilizing the μOR–G protein interface. This stabilization increases interfacial interactions and buried surface area, providing a G protein–dependent mechanism for enhanced efficacy despite increased agonist conformational flexibility and weakened orthosteric contacts. In contrast, the negative allosteric modulator compound 368 broadly enforces inactive-like microswitch conformations while simultaneously stabilizing antagonist binding. Unbinding kinetics simulations reveal that 368 exerts a dominant kinetic effect, restricting naloxone egress pathways and increasing residence time by approximately three orders of magnitude. Together, these results establish a unified framework in which μOR allostery operates through modulation of receptor and ligand conformational dynamics, G protein engagement, and ligand dissociation kinetics. This work provides an atomistic foundation for the rational design of next-generation opioid therapeutics that exploit allosteric mechanisms to enhance efficacy and safety.

item.title: Prediction of MOF Adsorption Isotherms and High-Throughput Screening Using a Physics-Informed Membranes Graph Neural Network
item.description: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are prime CO2-capture candidates, but grand canonical Monte Carlo (GCMC) screening is costly when full isotherms, not single uptakes, are required; machine learning surrogates rarely resolve the continuous pressure response. We report a physics-informed pressure-aware multi-task graph neural network (PI-MGNN) to predict CO2 uptake at arbitrary pressure and reconstruct isotherms from structure. From ~130,000 candidates, PCA and K-means select 5,023 representative MOFs, each simulated by GCMC at five pressures spanning 0.1-5.0 MPa, enforcing a continuous pressure response. Crystal graphs are processed by decoupled geometric and electrostatic graph-attention branches with auxiliary supervision, while a Gaussian-expanded pressure query is fused by cross-attention. PI-MGNN attains R2 = 0.977 and MAE = 0.291 mol kg-1; isotherm MAEs are 0.428/0.312/0.330 mol kg-1 for high/medium/low-uptake MOFs, and cross-attention improves accuracy by 6.3%. Attention weights recover the pressure-resolved physics, enabling accurate and interpretable high-throughput screening.

item.title: Depth-resolved operando grazing-incidence diffraction reveals non-equilibrium Cu-Pt alloy restructuring under glycerol electrooxidation
item.description: Alloying Pt with Cu enhances activity towards hydrogen generation and valueadded products during the electrooxidation of glycerol, but the most active alloys typically require electrochemical activation, during which their structure and composition evolve in poorly understood ways. Here we use synchrotron-based operando, angle-dependent grazing incidence X-ray diffraction in a custom dual-chamber electrochemical flow cell to follow, in real time, the depth-resolved structural evolution of Cu-Pt thin-film catalysts under glycerol electrooxidation in alkaline media. Our approach allows us to monitor the temporal evolution of lattice parameter, phase composition and microstrain during cyclic voltammetry and chronoamperometry while varying the X-ray penetration depth from the topmost tens of nanometres into the underlying alloy. For Cu-rich Cu92Pt8 catalysts, we observe substantial restructuring of the near-surface region, including the cyclic formation and reduction of Cu2O, pronounced Cu leaching from depths of several tens of nanometres, and the progressive emergence of a Pt-rich ≈Cu15Pt85 phase that stabilises the surface against further oxidation. These structural changes coincide with a ca. 5-fold increase in current density and a ca. 100 mV increase in onset potential during activation, after which the electrochemical response becomes stable. Pt-richer alloys exhibit markedly reduced restructuring, with compositional changes largely confined to the top ≈20-30 nm of the catalyst. Analysis of peak broadening via Williamson-Hall plots reveals that dealloying and surface oxidation are associated with increased microstrain, which subsequently relaxes as a Pt-rich surface configuration is established. Beyond revealing the non-equilibrium interplay of oxidation, segregation and realloying that governs the performance and durability of Cu-Pt catalysts for glycerol electrooxidation, our methodology and cell design provide a flexible, broadly applicable platform for operando, depth-resolved diffraction studies of electrochemical interfaces in energy and biomass-conversion reactions.

item.title: The helium ground-state energy to 60 significant figures on a laptop
item.description: We report a variational upper bound on the nonrelativistic, infinite-nuclear-mass ground-state energy of helium whose first 60 significant figures are converged, E0 = −2.903 724 377 034 119 598 311 159 245 194 404 446 696 925 311 117 290 339 042 34 Eh, 16 more than the best previous record. The calculation runs on a laptop and the method, which we call FLAKE (Fock-log anisotropic Kronecker eigensolver), combines four ingredients. (i) A change of variables making Schwartz’s Hylleraas-type basis with logarithms an exact tensor product, so the Hamiltonian is a sum of 27 Kronecker products of small matrices. (ii) Exact, arbitrary-precision orthonormalisation of the small radial and angular Gram factors removes all cancellation from the large computation. (iii) Fixed-point products at about 280 bits are split without error into ordinary double-precision matrix multiplications. (iv) The variational space is anisotropic: it carries extra radial degree and a tower of (ln s)p functions only at low angular order, as dictated by channelresolved convergence rates. Every energy quoted is certified by an independent arbitrary-precision evaluation of the Rayleigh quotient of the explicit trial function. The remaining error is estimated from geometric convergence laws that predicted subsequent energy increments to within 2%.

item.title: The Pnictogen Oracle Provider: Multi-Fidelity Graph Landscapes To Benchmark Molecular Optimization
item.description: The informed discovery and inverse design of new molecules and materials is among the most active applications of data-driven procedures, such as statistical learning, to chemical problems. These approaches involve two key aspects: the dataset, and the exploration algorithms. Here, we cover both of these dimensions by introducing POP (Pnictogen Oracle Provider), a platform comprised by an extensive graph database and an optimization toolkit. The database contains almost 200,000 structures for phosphines, amines and arsines at different fidelity levels, explicitly including failed calculations and enforcing a topology based on substituent-level mutation operations. On the other hand, the software toolkit streamlines the application of optimization algorithms (search policies and predictive oracles) to such databases, pushing forward the development of benchmarks. We explore the baseline application of a varied set of such methods—evolutionary algorithms, Bayesian Optimization, LLM-based procedures and multifidelity approaches—to the optimization of a key property: the HOMO-LUMO gap across each of the three ligand families. In this manner, we reveal the relevance of graph topology in the guidance of these algorithms, as well as the performance differences these baseline methods depending on the particularities of each of the ligand families.

item.title: Density Functional Theory Bond Dissociation Energies of Model Compounds Relevant to LDL Oxidation: Bis-Allylic C–H, Phenolic O–H and Hydroperoxide O–H Bonds
item.description: Background: Oxidative modification of low-density lipoprotein (LDL) contributes to atherogenesis, with polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) as its main chemical target. Vitamin E is an effective chain-breaking antioxidant in vitro, yet large clinical trials showed no cardiovascular benefit. We calculated bond dissociation energies (BDEs) of model compounds to quantify the underlying thermodynamics. Methods: Density functional theory calculations (PySCF; B3LYP/6-311+G(d,p)//B3LYP/6-31G*, scaled zero-point energy, 0 K) were performed for butane (secondary C–H), 1,4-pentadiene, phenol, catechol and methyl hydroperoxide. Vitamin E was not calculated at the relaxed level; published values were used. A truncated tocopherol model (5,7,8-trimethylchroman-6-ol) was run at screening level only (B3LYP/6-31+G*, unrelaxed geometries, no zero-point correction), with phenol at the same level. Results: The bis-allylic C–H bond of 1,4-pentadiene (68.2 kcal/mol) was 28.3 below the secondary C–H bond of butane (96.5). Catechol O–H (73.4) was 8.4 below phenol (81.8). The hydroperoxide model (79.6) fell 2.2 below phenol, whereas experimental values place the two within about 1 kcal/mol, comparable to their uncertainties, so phenol is a weak test of the order; catechol was 6.2 below the hydroperoxide, as expected. In screening calculations the tocopherol model was 9.0 below phenol. Published values place α-tocopherol O–H at about 77 to 78 kcal/mol, about 10 below phenol, the same direction as our screening gap. For the four bonds with experimental references, computed values were 1.7 to 8.6 kcal/mol below them; no direct experimental value exists for the bis-allylic C–H. Gaps and ordering, not absolute values, are therefore interpreted. Conclusions: The calculations quantify the thermodynamic basis for PUFA vulnerability and for the stronger hydrogen donation of polyphenol-type O–H bonds. They do not by themselves show donation to peroxyl radicals. Bond energies cannot explain the clinical trial results; kinetics, LDL localization and tocopherol-mediated peroxidation must be considered. No clinical outcomes or biomarkers were computed.

item.title: A Solution-Gated Graphene Transistor Sensor for the Detection and Quantification of Guanine Quadruplexes.
item.description: SGGT G4 Detection 2 ABSTRACT. We report the design, realization, and testing of a Solution-Gated Graphene Transistor Sensor aimed at detecting and quantifying guanine quadruplexes. By using all-atom molecular dynamic simulations complemented with free energy methods we rationally design the architecture of the sensors, exploiting an economic and easy-available G4 ligand. The prototype of the sensor has shown the capacity to provide a linear response depending on the G4 concentration, hence showing the proof of concept of its applicability for G4 detection. The proposed sensors may allow the rapid detection of guanine quadruplexes in complex matrices, without relying on the use of antibodies or complex experimental apparatus.

item.title: Development of A Modeling Framework for Characterizing Protein–Polymer Bioconjugates with Enhanced Sampling Molecular Dynamics Simulations
item.description: Protein–polymer bioconjugates represent a class of biomaterials that leverages the molecular specificity of proteins and the tunability of synthetic polymers. Strategic conjugation of polymers to protein surfaces can enhance key biomolecular properties such as structural stability and target affinity while preserving the biological functions of the native protein. The rational design of these hybrid biomolecules demands a detailed understanding of the underlying molecular mechanisms governing protein–polymer interfacial behavior. Critically, strong interfacial interactions can impose substantial energetic barriers that hinder conformational sampling in molecular dynamics (MD) studies of this system. Enhanced sampling methods are highly effective for overcoming such limitations in the simulation of biomolecular interfaces. However, the opportunity to apply enhanced sampling methods toward navigating the complex interfacial landscapes of protein–polymer bioconjugates has yet to be realized by the field. In this study, we showcase the development of a molecular modeling framework that leverages enhanced sampling to extensively characterize protein–polymer bioconjugates. To validate this framework, we constructed two bioconjugate models of hen egg-white lysozyme grafted with activated methoxy polyethylene glycol (mPEG) chains of varying lengths at multiple surface-exposed lysine sites. We then performed all-atom MD simulations of these PEGylated constructs, augmented with well-tempered metadynamics (WTM) to fully explore their conformational landscapes under multi-site polymer conjugation. This approach yielded converged free energy surfaces (FES) characterizing the thermodynamic favorability of grafted mPEG chain conformations at each conjugation site. We also identified key protein contact residues and site-specific non-bonded interactions responsible for bioconjugate stabilization. This study demonstrates a novel application of enhanced sampling methodologies in bioconjugate systems for characterizing site-specific conjugation effects on protein–polymer interfacial energetics and structural dynamics in the context of protein surface chemistry. More broadly, applying this methodological framework across diverse polymer chemistries and protein variants can elucidate molecular design rules for engineering bioconjugates with precise properties and functions for applications spanning biotechnology, energy, and health.

item.title: First-principles data for solid-solution Nb–Zr, Ta–Zr, and V–Zr binary alloys with body-centered-cubic structures
item.description: We present three open-access datasets containing density functional theory (DFT) calculations for refractory solid-solution binary alloys niobium–zirconium (NbZr), tantalum–zirconium (TaZr), and vanadium–zirconium (VZr) in 128-atom body-centered-cubic (BCC) supercells. These datasets extend our previously published first-principles collections for NbTa, NbV, TaV, and NbTaV alloys and were generated with the same automated high-throughput workflow based on the Vienna Ab-Initio Simulation Package (VASP). For each of the three NbZr, TaZr, and VZr systems, we uniformly sample 31 chemical compositions across the full composition range in 4-atom increments. For every composition we construct 100 distinct disordered atomic configurations by randomizing the element assignments on the BCC lattice sites. All structures are fully relaxed, and the released data include complete input files, detailed VASP outputs for each relaxation stage, and derived physical quantities such as ground-state formation energy and root mean-squared displacement (RMSD) relative to an ideal BCC reference. These Zr-containing binaries are motivated by our earlier demonstration that graph neural networks (GNNs) trained on binary NbTa, NbV, and TaV data can interpolate formation enthalpies and structural descriptors in ternary NbTaV alloys while dramatically reducing the required number of ternary DFT calculations. The new NbZr, TaZr, and VZr datasets increase the diversity of available binary training data, in particular in systems with larger size mismatch and stronger lattice distortion due to Zr, and are intended to support the development of transferable machine learning (ML) interatomic models for accelerated exploration of high-dimensional multicomponent alloy spaces.

item.title: A soluble conductive chromium coordination polymer with radical ligands and non-integer redox states
item.description: There are few conductive metal-organic materials that are solution processible or that feature electron-accepting conductive units. Thus, a soluble, semiconductive coordination polymer (1n+)x (n = 1 – 3) was developed by linking CrIII ions with electron-deficient back-to-back bis-terpyridine (btpy) ligands.
